extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, third-party requesters, and USPTO examiners/practitioners handling inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements governing Board decisions, new grounds of rejection, requests for rehearing or reopening prosecution, remands, appeals, and disclosure duties in inter partes reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to file responsive comments on request for rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third party requester that is a party to the appeal may, within a non-extendable one month period from the date of service of the request for rehearing, file responsive comments on the request for rehearing. See 37 CFR 41.79(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This one-month period may not be extended. See 37 CFR 41.79(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Board decision on rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where at least one request for rehearing of the decision is granted, the Board’s decision on the request for rehearing is deemed to incorporate the earlier opinion reflecting its decision for appeal, except for those portions specifically withdrawn on rehearing, and the decision is final for the purpose of judicial review, except when noted otherwise in the decision on rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board opinion on rehearing indicates a new decision, any party may, within one month of the new decision, file a further request for rehearing that must comply with 37 CFR 41.79(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if Board decision not timely appealed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board’s final decision on the request for rehearing is not timely appealed to the court, jurisdiction of the case is returned to the CRU for processing and subsequent forwarding to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will proceed to issue a NIRC and terminate prosecution of the reexamination proceeding. See 37 CFR 1.979(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may make new ground(s) of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 41.77(b), the Board may, in its decision on appeal, make a new rejection of one or more appealed claims on either the same grounds with different reasoning or on different grounds from those applied against the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reversal constitutes a decision adverse to patentability of claims (e.g., reversal of examiner's refusal), it will be set forth as a new ground of rejection under 37 CFR 41.77(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner options after a Board new-ground decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After a decision under 37 CFR 41.77(b) the patent owner must, within one month from the date of the decision, either (A) request rehearing based upon the same record under 37 CFR 41.79(a); or (B) file a response requesting reopening prosecution before the examiner including an appropriate amendment of the newly rejected claim(s), and/or new evidence relating to the new ground(s) of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may not file both a response requesting reopening and also a request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.79(a) for the same decision; extensions of time are available under 37 CFR 1.956 where reopening will be requested; no extensions are available to request rehearing. See 37 CFR 41.77(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: No immediate appeal to Federal Circuit after new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: After a decision under 37 CFR 41.77(b), the parties do not have the option of an immediate appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit because the decision under 37 CFR 41.77(b) is not a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must first exercise one of the permitted options (rehearing or reopening) within the one month period; only after the process is finalized may further appeal routes be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board termination if patent owner fails to act
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner does not exercise either permitted option (rehearing or requesting reopening), then the Board may terminate the appeal as to the newly rejected claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner files a submission under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1) or (2) that is denied entry by the Board, then the Board may terminate the appeal as to the newly rejected claim(s), designate the decision as to any remaining claims as a final decision, and permit a request for rehearing for the affirmed claims within one month from the date of notice of termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction remains with Board until remand or final designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of the proceeding remains with the Board until the Board (1) remands the proceeding to the examiner or (2) designates the decision as a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after a remand or final designation does jurisdiction shift; remands and finality affect subsequent procedural options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may not sua sponte reopen prosecution or issue NIRC after Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not, sua sponte, reopen prosecution, or issue a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) after a Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening must follow the procedures set by the Board and applicable CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing both rehearing and reopening (including conditional requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may not file both a response requesting a reopening of prosecution and also a request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.79(a) for the same decision. A patent owner may also not file both a request for rehearing and a conditional request to reopen in the event that the request for rehearing is denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an improper conditional request to reopen prosecution is received, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1), and the request for rehearing will not be entered or considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for requests after new-ground decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner seeking to request one of the permitted options must comply with the timing provisions set forth in 37 CFR 41.77(g) and 41.79(a)(2), both of which run from the date of the original decision of the Board under 37 CFR 41.77(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.956 may be available when reopening is requested, but such extensions cannot extend beyond six months from the date of the Board’s decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-month period for rehearing under 41.77(b)(2) and waiver of further prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner’s request for rehearing by the Board must be filed within a non-extendable one month period set by 37 CFR 41.79(a). By proceeding in this manner, the patent owner waives his or her right to further prosecution before the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner files a request for rehearing, any third party requester that is a party to the appeal may, within a non-extendable one month period from the date of service of the request for rehearing, file responsive comments under 37 CFR 41.79(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for reopening prosecution under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner elects to proceed before the examiner, the patent owner must take action within the one month period for response which will be set in the Board’s decision. The patent owner may amend the claims involved, substitute new claims to avoid the art or reasons stated by the Board, and/or submit evidence relating to the new rejection(s) set forth by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.956 are available but may not extend more than six months from the Board's decision. Mere argument without either amendment or submission of evidence/showing of facts is not in compliance and the Board will not grant the request to reopen. Any amendment or evidence not directed to the subject matter to which the new rejection was applied will be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party comments under 37 CFR 41.77(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester may once file comments on the patent owner’s submission under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1) within one month of the date of service of the request to reopen prosecution. The one-month time period cannot be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be limited to issues concerning the new ground(s) of rejection raised by the Board or the patent owner’s response; may include new evidence and arguments if limited to supporting the new grounds (including evidence directed to amended/new claims if necessitated). Comments addressing issues not raised by the new grounds will be refused entry. If the third party is not an appellant or cross-appellant, comments may still be filed only with payment of the appeal and appeal brief fees per 37 CFR 41.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand order should indicate entry status of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board formally remands the proceeding back to the examiner, the remand order should indicate whether the patent owner’s response under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1) is entered, not entered, or entered-in-part; and similarly explain whether any third party requester comments were entered or entered-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should assume the Board has entered papers filed under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1) or (c) unless the remand order explicitly states otherwise. If uncertain, the examiner should discuss with SPRS who may contact the Board for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limitation of examiner’s determination under 37 CFR 41.77(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: After remand, the examiner may only issue a determination under 37 CFR 41.77(d); the determination is limited to whether or not the new statutory ground(s) of rejection in the Board decision has been overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will explain reasoning, explicitly identify any limitation not taught by applied references, and address any entered third-party arguments/evidence. The examiner will not issue other types of Office actions (nonfinal, advisory, Right of Appeal Notice, or NIRC) and will not comment on unentered amendments/arguments/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods set by examiner’s determination under 37 CFR 41.77(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination will set (1) a one-month time period from the mailing date of the determination for the patent owner and third party requester(s) to file comments on the examiner’s determination under 37 CFR 41.77(d) and (2) a one month time period from date of service of such comments for replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These time periods cannot be extended. See 37 CFR 41.77(e) and form paragraph example (¶ 26.75).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments and replies under 37 CFR 41.77(e) — scope and entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner and third party requester(s) have one month from the mailing date of the determination under 37 CFR 41.77(d) to once file comments on the determination; opposing parties may file a single reply. No amendments or further evidence may be submitted as part of these comments or replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies must be filed within one month from service of the comments. Time periods cannot be extended. Examiner will review for compliance similar to rebuttal brief review (MPEP §2678); non-compliant comments/replies will not be entered but will remain in the record and the examiner will notify the parties and Board (e.g., PTOL-90). If no comments/replies are filed, examiner returns the proceeding to the Board for action under 37 CFR 41.77(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board action after examiner determination and comments (37 CFR 41.77(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt and compliance review of any comments and replies, the examiner forwards the proceeding to the Board, and jurisdiction transfers to the Board which will then act under 37 CFR 41.77(f); if the Board issues a final decision, parties have the alternatives available following a final decision by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications (e.g., PTOL-90) will state which submissions were entered and that the proceeding is being forwarded to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by Board under 37 CFR 41.77(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may remand the case to an examiner where appropriate procedure has not been followed, where further information is needed, or where the examiner is to consider something which the examiner did not yet consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board remand is not a final decision. After the examiner addresses the remand, the examiner will either return the case to the Board (via the CRU) or reopen prosecution as appropriate; reopening after Board decision should be rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for reopening prosecution after remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings decided by the Board will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner unless the provisions of 37 CFR 41.77 apply, or the written consent of the Director of the USPTO is obtained for consideration of matters not already adjudicated where sufficient cause is shown (see 37 CFR 1.981).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written consent of the CRU Director is required for an action reopening prosecution where the examiner concludes a decision in the RAN should be changed; CRU Director will decide any petition to reopen prosecution after jurisdiction returns to the CRU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Federal Circuit — procedural steps
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner or third party requester who is in an inter partes reexamination proceeding and dissatisfied with a final Board decision may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit by (1) timely filing a written notice of appeal in the Office directed to the Director in accordance with §§ 1.302 and 1.304; (2) filing a copy of the notice of appeal and paying the fee in the Federal Circuit; and (3) serving a copy of the notice of appeal on every other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided in § 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 41.81 the Board decision must be final and all rehearing rights exhausted before appeal; specific cross-appeal and participation rules (including 14-day participation notices) apply. For proceedings commenced prior to Nov 2, 2002, third party requester may be precluded from appealing/cross-appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing notice of appeal or commencing civil action (37 CFR 1.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing the notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or for commencing a civil action is two months from the date of the decision of the Board. If a request for rehearing is filed, the time for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action shall expire two months after action on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time periods are calendar days/months; these times are not subject to § 1.136, § 1.550(c), § 1.956, or § 41.4. The Director may extend for good cause if requested in writing before expiration, or upon showing of excusable neglect after expiration; special calendaring rules for February and weekends/holidays apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and cross-appeal in Federal Circuit appeals (37 CFR 1.983)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party electing to participate in an appellant’s appeal must, within fourteen days of service of the appellant’s notice of appeal or notice of cross appeal, timely file a written notice directed to the Director electing to participate, file a copy in the Federal Circuit per its rules, and serve a copy on every other party per § 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requester may cross-appeal if patent owner has appealed and vice versa, subject to statutory limitations for proceedings commenced before certain dates; participation notices should provide sufficient information to allow the Director to consider intervention under 35 U.S.C. 143.

rubrics_metrics.name: No remedy by civil action in inter partes reexamination (35 U.S.C. 145)
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedy by civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 is not available to the patent owner and the third party requester in an inter partes reexamination proceeding; they are limited to appeal to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inter partes reexamination alternative was added, the statute did not provide the parties an avenue of judicial review by civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 for inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.933)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination proceeding has a duty of candor and good faith in dealing with the Office, which includes a duty to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability in a reexamination proceeding as set forth in § 1.555(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty is deemed satisfied by filing a paper in compliance with § 1.555(a) and (b). Responsibility for compliance rests on the designated individuals and the Office will not evaluate compliance in the reexamination proceeding; unresolved questions will be noted per § 1.906(c). Duty of disclosure considerations parallel ex parte reexamination proceedings.
